texts.li: [lowtech] A few healers of {FACTION} have come down the road with packs of dried herbs and a mule loaded with pots. {X_nameDef}, the eldest, told {A_nameDef} they go from village to village seeing to whatever needs seeing to, and they'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few days.

[!lowtech] A traveling clinic of {FACTION} has stopped by the colony: a handful of medics, a folding table and a crate of supplies. {X_nameDef}, who runs it, told {A_nameDef} they'll set up {PLACE} for a few days and see anyone who needs seeing.

[ws:sickness] Healers of {FACTION} are on the roads because of {SITUATION}, going wherever they're needed. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'd like to rest {PLACE} for a few days, and will see to anyone at the colony who's ailing while they're here.

[winter] Healers of {FACTION} came in out of the cold with frost on their packs. Winter is their busiest season, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}: coughs, chilblains, falls on the ice. They'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few days and rest before the next village.

Healers of {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land with a cart of remedies and a sign that says, in three languages, that they ask no questions. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} a few days, and the colony is welcome at their table.

settled.li: The healers from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}: a fire, a table of remedies and a torch to work by after dark.
[lowtech] The healers from {FACTION} have hung bundles of herbs to dry around their fire {PLACE}, and the smell of them carries to the colony.
[!lowtech] The healers from {FACTION} have set out their table {PLACE}, with bottles in neat rows and a clean cloth over the instruments.
The healers from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a pot of something simmering that smells like medicine and a bench for the sick to wait on.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the healers camped {PLACE}, says the colony has more need of a healer than the road does, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay.
{X_nameDef} from the healers' camp has been seeing to the colonists' scrapes and coughs every evening, unasked. Tonight {X_nameDef} asked whether there might be a place for a healer here, for good.
{X_nameDef}, the youngest of the healers {PLACE}, has been learning the colony's names and complaints by heart, and asks whether a healer might be wanted here for good.

farewell.li: The healers from {FACTION} packed up their remedies and went on to the next village, with a long list of the colony's coughs to ask about next time.
The healers' camp {PLACE} is gone, and the smell of drying herbs with it. {X_nameDef} left a jar of salve on the gatepost.
The healers from {FACTION} left at dawn. {X_nameDef} went round the colony first, checking on everyone they'd treated.

helpTexts.li: [heal] {X_nameDef} from the healers' camp caught {A_nameDef} at the well and saw to {A_possessive} {THING} there and then, with a poultice and a cup of something bitter. {A_nameDef} is already feeling better.

[heal,lowtech] {X_nameDef}, the eldest of the healers, sat {A_nameDef} down by the camp's fire and saw to the {THING} with herbs and a lot of muttering. {A_nameDef} came back to the colony looking much brighter.
[heal,!lowtech] {X_nameDef} from the clinic {PLACE} took one look at {A_nameDef}'s {THING}, sat {A_objective} down at the folding table, and dealt with it in twenty minutes. No charge.
[herbs] The healers {PLACE} had herbs to spare, and left {COUNT} bundles of herbal medicine where the colony can collect them.
[herbs] {X_nameDef} from the healers' camp came by with {COUNT} bundles of dried healroot for the colony's stores, and a long lecture on how to keep them dry.

texts.li: A procession of {FACTION} has come singing up the road behind a carried shrine: the faithful of a dozen villages, bound for a holy place far beyond the colony. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might rest {PLACE} for a few days and keep their prayers.

[ideology] Followers of {IDEO} from {FACTION} have come up the road carrying the relics of their faith on poles. {X_nameDef}, who walks at the front, asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE}, to rest and to pray.

[ideology,sameFaith] A procession of {FACTION} has arrived singing hymns the colony knows: they keep {IDEO}, the colony's own faith, and they've come out of their way to rest among their own. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE}.

[ws:faith] {SITUATION} has brought the faithful out on every road, and a procession of {FACTION} has stopped by the colony on its way. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} for a few days.

[lowtech] A procession of {FACTION} has come over the hill with bells and drums, carrying a carved figure on a litter. {X_nameDef}, their leader, asked {A_nameDef} whether the figure and its people might rest {PLACE} a few nights on their long road.

settled.li: The faithful from {FACTION} have set their shrine down {PLACE}, with a place cleared before it for prayer and their bedrolls in a ring around the fire.
[ideology] The followers of {IDEO} have made their camp {PLACE}. Their relics stand on a cloth near the cookpot, and someone is always keeping watch over them.
The faithful from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, the shrine set facing the sunrise and their bells hung on a pole beside it.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the faithful camped {PLACE}, says the road has brought {X_objective} where {X_pronoun} was meant to be, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay with the colony instead of walking on.
[sameFaith] {X_nameDef} from the procession {PLACE} has found people of {X_possessive} own faith here, and asks, after a night's prayer about it, to stay.
{X_nameDef}, one of the faithful camped {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} has carried the shrine far enough, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might set down {X_possessive} load here, among the colony.

farewell.li: The procession from {FACTION} lifted its shrine at dawn and went on singing up the road. The colony could hear them long after they'd gone out of sight.
The faithful from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} and went on toward their holy place. {X_nameDef} said they'd pray for the colony there.
The procession from {FACTION} went on its way, bells ringing, leaving a small offering of bread at the colony's gate.

lines.li: Sing it again, from the start.

helpTexts.li: [blessing] {X_nameDef}, the eldest of the faithful, came to the colony at dusk and walked its paths with a bell, blessing the houses, the fields and the people one by one.
[blessing,ideology] The followers of {IDEO} came to the colony's gate at sunset and sang a blessing over it, the whole procession together, before going back to their fire.
[blessing,sameFaith] The procession came to the colony this evening to pray with it, as people of one faith. {X_nameDef} led the prayers, and {A_nameDef} stood at the front.
[blessing,lowtech] The faithful carried their shrine around the colony's fields at dusk, ringing bells, so the land would be kind to the people working it.

texts.li: [lowtech] A troupe of {FACTION}'s players has come up the road with a painted wagon and a dancing goat. {X_nameDef}, who does the talking, told {A_nameDef} they'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few nights and put on shows for anyone who comes, for whatever anyone wants to give.

[!lowtech] A small circus of {FACTION} has pulled up by the colony: a handful of performers, a striped tent rolled up on a trailer, and a juggler who hasn't stopped juggling since they arrived. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} for a few nights and perform every evening.

Players of {FACTION} have stopped at the colony with costumes in a trunk and a play they're tired of. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} if they could camp {PLACE} for a few nights, rehearse something new, and try it out on the colony.

[winter] Players of {FACTION} came in out of the snow in their stage clothes, which are warmer than they look. There are no audiences on the roads in winter, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}; they'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few nights and play for the colony instead.

[tribal] Dancers and drummers of {FACTION} have come to the colony, painted for the dance. They travel from camp to camp and dance the old stories, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and would like to stay {PLACE} a few nights.

settled.li: The players from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a stage of packed earth and a torch at each corner.
[!lowtech] The circus from {FACTION} has strung lanterns between two poles {PLACE} and marked out a ring in the dirt. The juggler is still juggling.
[tribal] The dancers from {FACTION} have cleared a dancing ground {PLACE} and beaten it flat. Their drums are already going at dusk.
The players from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, costumes hung on a line to air and a trunk of props open by the fire.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the players camped {PLACE}, is tired of the road and of sleeping in a different field every week, and asks whether the colony has room for someone who can sing, juggle and lift heavy things.
{X_nameDef} from the players' camp has been coming to the colony's supper table more than the camp's. Tonight {X_nameDef} asked, with a bow, whether {X_pronoun} might stay.
{X_nameDef}, who plays the villains for the troupe camped {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} would like to be nobody's villain for a while, and asks to stay.

farewell.li: The players from {FACTION} packed their costumes into the trunk and went on to the next town, waving from the wagon until they were out of sight.
The players' camp {PLACE} is empty, except for a painted backdrop of a castle they decided they didn't need.
The players from {FACTION} took a last bow at the gate and went on to the next town, still arguing about the second act.

lines.li: Louder, they can't hear you at the back.

helpTexts.li: [show] The players {PLACE} put on a play at their fire this evening, a comedy about a lord who loses his trousers, and the colony was invited. {X_nameDef} played the lord.
[show,!lowtech] The circus {PLACE} put on its full show tonight: juggling, a tightrope between two poles, and a strongman who lifted {A_nameDef} over his head. The colony laughed itself hoarse.
[show,tribal] The dancers {PLACE} danced the story of the first hunt tonight, round the fire, with the colony watching from the dark. {X_nameDef} danced the beast.
[show,lowtech] The mummers {PLACE} played the old story of the fool and the dragon tonight, and {X_nameDef}'s dragon chased the colony's children all round the fire.
[show] The players camped {PLACE} tried out their new play on the colony tonight. It needs work, {X_nameDef} says. The colony clapped anyway.

texts.li: [medieval] Surveyors of {FACTION}, with chains, measuring rods and a great deal of string, have come onto the colony's land. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} their lord wants the whole valley mapped, and they'll camp {PLACE} for a few days while they do this part of it.

[industrial|spacer] Surveyors of {FACTION} have set up a tripod on the ridge and are squinting at the colony through it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they're mapping the region for {FACTION}'s charts, and would like to camp {PLACE} for a few days.

[ws:road] {SITUATION} needs a line through the hills, and surveyors of {FACTION} have come to find it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} for a few days, and will keep their stakes off the colony's fields.

[ws:rush] With everyone in the region talking about {SITUATION}, {FACTION} have sent surveyors to map the rock properly. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'd like to camp {PLACE} a few days, and will share what they find in the colony's hills.

settled.li: The surveyors from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a windbreak against the weather and their instruments wrapped in oilcloth.
The surveyors' camp {PLACE} is up, with a torch to work their figures by at night and a line of stakes running off into the hills.
The surveyors from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, maps weighted down with stones and a long cord marked off in paces coiled by the fire.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the surveyors' camp has walked every hill around the colony and decided {X_pronoun} likes this one best. {X_nameDef} asks whether the colony would take on someone who knows rock and distances.
{X_nameDef}, the surveyors' youngest, has been sketching the colony instead of the land, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and draw it properly.

farewell.li: The surveyors from {FACTION} pulled up their stakes and went on to map the next valley, leaving a copy of their sketch of the colony's land pinned to the gate.
The surveyors' camp {PLACE} is gone. Somewhere in {FACTION}'s charts, the colony is a small careful square with its name beside it.
The surveyors from {FACTION} left before breakfast, carrying the colony's hills away with them on paper.

lines.li: Three hundred paces. Write it down.
That hill's in the wrong place.

helpTexts.li: [survey] {X_nameDef} from the surveyors' camp has been studying the colony's rock, and walked {A_nameDef} out to show {A_objective} a seam of {THING} the colony never knew was there.
[survey,industrial|spacer] The surveyors {PLACE} ran their instruments over the colony's hills for a day, and {X_nameDef} came back with a marked map: a seam of {THING}, close to the surface.
[survey,medieval] {X_nameDef}, the surveyors' master, has a nose for ore. A morning of tapping at the rock with a jeweler's hammer, and {X_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} a seam of {THING}.

li.label: a healer from the camp saw to me
li.description: One of the healers camped nearby saw I was poorly and saw to it, for nothing. I feel better already.

li.label: a show at the camp
li.description: The people camped nearby put on a show at their fire, and we were all invited. I laughed until it hurt.

li.label: blessed by the faithful
li.description: The faithful camped nearby came and blessed the colony. Whatever it's worth, it was kindly meant.
